title: Dynamic data acquisition in PET diagnostics: a prospective data collection in clinically indicated examinations
summary:
Combined positron emission tomography with computed tomography (PET/CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI) plays a crucial role in imaging diagnostics in many cancers. This applies both, in the initial diagnosis and in the monitoring of the disease under therapy. Even with inflammatory diseases - such as vasculitis - PET/CT improves diagnosis and can save patients from having to take painful tissue samples (biopsies) with side effects.
However, an exact differentiation between cancer and inflammatory processes or tissue changes after therapy remains a major challenge in routine clinical practice. Many of these changes are associated with non-specific tracer uptake, this means the usually sugar metabolism measured by PET cannot always differentiate inflammation from tumor well enough. This is especially true if only so-called static images are available in the PET/CT or PET/MRI measurement, which usually analyse the metabolism 60 minutes after administration of the radiotracer.
In the planned diagnostic study, dynamic PET parameters of the whole body are to be collected, analyzed and correlated with tissue data from the pathological examination and the course of the disease. For this, we will use the so called  multi-bed multi-timepoint technique based on a larger representative patient population. The aim of this study is to get a better distinction between inflammation and tumor events.
conditions: Inflammatory forms of disease (e.g. fever of unclear origin, vasculitis, spondylodiscitis or unclear inflammation in the chest / pulmonary etc.)
Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined sites in the lip, oral cavity and pharynx
Malignant neoplasm, without specification of site
Other and unspecified types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
Other disorders of arteries and arterioles

interventions.name:
Patients with oncological or inflammatory disease who, due to the study, also acquire dynamic PET data in addition to their clinically indicated PET/CT or PET/MRT in static recording mode.
The PET parameters collected are correlated with histopathological findings and the course of the disease.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Clinical indication for a PET/CT or PET/MRI examination
• Patients with a malignant or inflammatory disease
• Patients who are able to understand the nature and scope of the pseudonymized, prospective data collection
• Patients who tolerate 80 min measuring time in the PET/CT scanner
• Age ≥18 years
• Written consent of the patient
Exclusion criteria:
• Pregnant and lactating women,
• Patients with claustrophobia,
• Patients with problems/pain when lying on their back, who may not tolerate a measurement time of more than one hour,
• Exclusion criteria according to the Radiation Protection Ordinance (StrlSchV),
• The patient's limited ability to consent.
